Ethos & Values

Ethos & Values
Clarendon School is a day special school for 140 pupils (50 Primary and 90 Secondary) aged 4-16yrs with learning difficulties (usually within the moderate range) and additional complex needs.
The school is part of the continuum created to meet special educational needs within the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames. The ethos of the school reflects the importance that we place on academic, social and emotional development.
Our emphasis is on developing individual potential whilst fostering caring and positive attitudes. Students participate in a full range of academic and social activities (class size of approx 12), and follow all the subjects of the National Curriculum. Clubs to suit all interests are organised after school at the Secondary Centre.
We have a team of staff that provide additional therapy sessions: speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, behaviour support, music therapy, counselling, art therapy and family therapy, all of which contribute towards individual student development
Our Vision
Our Mission
Clarendon School became part of Helix Learning Trust in September 2026, following the merger of Auriga Academy Trust and Coombe Academy Trust. As part of Helix Learning Trust, we work collaboratively with colleagues across our family of mainstream and specialist schools, sharing expertise, resources and best practice to improve outcomes for all learners. Together, we are committed to the Trust's shared values of Trust, Ambition and Collaboration, while maintaining Clarendon's unique specialist identity and inclusive ethos.
In a nurturing, safe and engaging environment.
British Values
At Clarendon we promote ‘British Values’ through our spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) education which permeates through the school’s curriculum and supports the development of the whole child. We recognise that such development is most successful when those values and attitudes are promoted by all the staff and provide a model of behaviour for our pupils.
The curriculum in all phases offers broad and balanced opportunities for each of the British Values:
Democracy The ability to understand and communicate are the most important areas of learning. We ensure that pupils are given a ‘voice’ to communicate. This ‘voice’ could be using words, objects, photographs, pictures or symbols.
We empower our pupils by giving them opportunities to make choices about the things that they believe to be important. By valuing each ‘voice’ and by listening and responding to that voice we demonstrate that we support democracy and liberty. We have an active School Council, elected by the pupils.
The Rule of Law We involve pupils in setting codes of behaviour; helping pupils to make decisions and choices that are acceptable to the school community and society at large. Pupils are helped to learn to manage their behaviour and take responsibility for their actions. Staff are committed to providing a consistent and predictable environment within the school and beyond. We can help some pupils to understand the connection between actions and consequences. This type of environment enables pupils to feel safe and secure; this in turn, promotes the optimum conditions for learning to take place.
Individual Liberty Pupils are encouraged to become good and valued citizens. We do this by supporting each pupil to become as independent as possible. We endeavour to demonstrate that everyone has rights; this includes the right to say 'Yes' or 'No' to ideas or activities. Some pupils will be able to take responsibility for particular roles and to understand that with certain rights comes a level of responsibility. Learning to do things independently is an important part of learning to understand yourself. We support others by participating in charitable events such as Red Nose Day/Comic Relief and Children in Need. We believe that engendering a caring and helpful environment and being independent can boost and nurture a healthy self-esteem.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs We promote each pupil's inclusion in activities, settings and locations that are appropriate to them individually to meet their needs. Within school, pupils work with a range of people and interactions with others are always positively promoted on a personalised basis for each individual. This includes respecting the different faiths and beliefs of others as well as persons of no faith. Our curriculum is planned to support understanding and tolerance across our community.
Approach We believe it is important to facilitate opportunities to be part of the community as the pupils, families and staff have much to offer in the development of community cohesion.
We integrate these values alongside spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) development through the themes of our assemblies programme. Our assemblies are inclusive of those of all faiths and none, helping all pupils to find out about themselves and others while linking their lives to their communities. The themes cover areas such as: friendships, helping others and celebrations from a range of faiths and world events and awareness days.
The staff work closely with parents, carers and other professionals to ensure that the pupils at Clarendon School are happy, well cared for and enabled to learn the skills they need to live a fulfilling life as part of their community.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Clarendon School. A place of learning for everyone.
Hello and welcome to Clarendon School. We are a successful and highly inclusive Special School meeting the needs of pupils aged 4 to 16 with Moderate Learning Difficulties, many of whom have additional complex needs including autism. We proudly believe that Clarendon is:
"a place of learning for everyone"
We currently operate across three wonderful sites: our Primary Centre in Hampton, our Secondary Centre in Twickenham, and our highly inclusive Gateway Centre based in Whitton. Like all thriving schools, we are growing together and have exciting plans for the future. In September 2026, we will be opening our brand-new Clarendon Riverside Centre in Petersham, expanding our capacity and extending our outstanding provision to young adults up to age 19.
Our ambitious curriculum is carefully designed to meet the unique profiles of our learners. It remains flexible so we can provide bespoke learning opportunities that focus not only on academic achievement—offering pathways to Entry Level and Functional Skills qualifications — but also heavily emphasise independence, communication, and essential life skills.
In September 2026, Clarendon School became part of Helix Learning Trust, following the merger of Auriga Academy Trust and Coombe Academy Trust. We continue to work closely with colleagues across the Trust and with external partners, sharing expertise and best practice to provide the very best education and support for our learners. Our experienced staff work collaboratively to deliver a nurturing, total communication environment, integrating academic, social and therapeutic provision, supported by a wide range of specialists including Occupational Therapists and Speech and Language Therapists.
We have high expectations of everyone at Clarendon School and firmly believe that by working in close partnership with families, we can provide an exceptional education for every learner. We provide a safe, nurturing environment that encourages challenge, celebrates achievement and supports every young person to reach their full potential.
With the skills, knowledge, and resilience learned over their time at Clarendon School, our students will leave fully prepared for their next steps in education or employment, ready to play a meaningful part in society.
With the skills, knowledge and resilience developed during their time at Clarendon School, our students leave fully prepared for their next steps in further education, employment or adult life, ready to make a positive and meaningful contribution to their communities.

Careers and IAG
Careers Education Statement
At Clarendon School, we are committed to providing a robust and sustainable careers programme that is carefully tailored to the individual needs of our students, particularly those with Moderate Learning Difficulties (MLD).
Parents/Carers
Parents and carers are actively encouraged to play a vital role in supporting their child’s career decisions through our school’s annual review process. In addition to the personal guidance mentioned above, we recommend parents to explore labour market information using various career search websites. While the school supports securing work placements, parents are encouraged to assist their child in finding placements where possible.
Employers
Clarendon School welcomes the opportunity to engage with prospective employers who are willing to share their expertise and help build our students' knowledge of employability skills, the workplace, the labour market, and job search strategies. Your input brings our careers programme to life and has a lasting impact on our students, helping them to develop essential skills for future success. If you would like to participate in one of our events or contribute to our careers programme, please get in touch with the school.
Careers Programme
Our comprehensive programme for all students is consistent with the eight Gatsby benchmarks, ensuring every learner receives high-quality careers education, information, advice, and guidance (IAG).

Our goal is to equip every student with the skills, confidence, and knowledge they need to succeed beyond Clarendon School, preparing them for meaningful and productive futures.

Ofsted
"You have created a school where leaders, governors and staff have the highest ambition for all pupils. They make excellent progress in all classes and all key stages" - Ofsted January 2019
The academic ethos of Clarendon is based on the idea that high standards and improvements in pupil performances are more likely to be achieved within an environment that is nurturing, encouraging and supportive while at the same time setting challenges. The more able and independent will relish the challenges while aware that support is available when they run into difficulty. The less able and less independent will make better progress and gain in confidence with the active assistance of the staff.
If the challenges and the support are to be accurately targeted it is essential that there is an effective system for monitoring and assessing pupil progress. If pupils are to respond positively to the teaching they receive they must be given praise and encouragement for the effort and progress that they make at whatever academic level they are operating. This needs to vary from encouraging remarks and praise given by their teacher to public acknowledgement of their success.
"Parents and carers hold the school in high regard and value the improvements they see in their children’s level of confidence and overall academic performance" - Ofsted 2019

Gateway Team
The Gateway Centre is led by Miss Jayne Gray. She has worked at the Gateway centre for a number of years as a qualified teacher and has a masters in special and inclusive education alongside numerous qualifications and certificates in autism, dyslexia and special educational needs.
There are two teachers who take responsibility for overseeing the curriculum and progress for key stage three and key stage four. They also run interventions for students during Gateway sessions and oversee subjects which are taught outside of the mainstream school. In addition, they teach specialist courses within the Gateway Centre for students on a more vocational pathway at key stage 4 which they plan and deliver, this includes CoPE.
We have one specialist keyworker who has undertaken numerous training courses in autism and is currently embarking on the ELSA course who can deliver curriculum content and specialises in emotional literacy and interventions.
There are nine keyworkers who work at the Gateway Centre supporting students. Each student is allocated a keyworker who liaises with parents and builds a strong relationship with their key student to help both facilitate learning and support students as they mature. Keyworkers undertake training yearly including courses in autism and other associated difficulties.
The Gateway centre has a fully qualified music therapist who works one day a week with individual students. Also, a speech and language therapist attends the Gateway centre weekly and provides staff training, as well as delivering joint sessions with students and offering consultations for keyworkers already delivering programmes of work.
The Gateway is currently being audited by Occupational Therapy to determine the level of service which needs to be delivered to the Gateway Centre.

School Fund
Schools everywhere are facing significant funding pressures. Rising costs and static or decreasing budgets mean that it is increasingly difficult to provide the enriching opportunities and additional resources that help pupils thrive.
These are often the areas hit hardest, yet they are the very things that make school an inspiring and enjoyable place for our children.
To help protect these opportunities, we have a Clarendon School Fund made up of voluntary contributions from parents and carers. This fund supports workshops, special events, software, classroom resources, and equipment — the “extras” that go beyond the basics and make a real difference to our pupils’ experience.
The School Fund gives you the opportunity to make either a one-off donation or a regular contribution that suits your budget. We are very aware of the many financial pressures on families, so we are genuinely grateful for anything you feel able to contribute. Your support really does make a difference to what we can offer our students.
Thank you very much for your generosity and for being part of the Clarendon community. For further information, please see below.
How do I contribute?
Contributions can be made using the following methods:
Standing Order: Please set up a monthly standing order to this bank account:
The Helix Learning Trust
Account number 84560360
Please quote reference: CLA donate + your suname
Parent Pay: It is possible to donate through Arbor using the School Shop. Simply log in to your Arbor app and navigate to the School Shop.
Scan the QR code: Scan below if you wish to make a donation or click the link
Make a donation click here
You will be given the option to gift aid. In the message section, please state your name so we know who has made the donation. Leave it blank if you wish to remain anonymous.
Bank Transfer: Bank transfers can be made for one off donations to:
The Helix Learning Trust
Account number 84560360
Please quote reference: CLA donate + your suname
Can I gift aid my payment
Academy trusts, as exempt charities, are eligible to claim Gift Aid on voluntary donations made by UK taxpayers.
Gift Aid allows the Trust to reclaim the basic rate of income tax on donations for all schools within the Trust, effectively increasing the value of eligible donations by 25% at no extra cost to the donor. For every £1 you donate, we can get an extra 25p from HMRC at no extra cost to you. Find out more on the Gov.uk webiste:
If you are a UK taxpayer, please email the school office to receive a Gift Aid Form. info@clarendon.richmond.sch.ukOr complete the Gift Aid Form link, which will be forwarded on to the Trust finance team. Gift Aid Form
How much should I contribute?
This is up to you and depends on your personal circumstances. For regular monthly contributions, we suggest between £10 and £20 per month, but we ask those parents and carers who can afford it to give more, please.
If you are a UK taxpayer, we politely request a minimum monthly donation of £10 or a minimum one-off donation of £50 to keep the administration of the Gift Aid scheme justifiable. However, we are very grateful for any amount you can give via the non-Gift Aid account.
Will my child be affected if I cannot pay?
The donation is voluntary and confidential; not making a payment will not affect your child in any way.
Thank you for supporting Clarendon School.

Secondary Centre Assessment and Results
There are annual standardised tests in reading, spelling and maths for all secondary pupils.
Pupils are teacher assessed in all aspects of English and maths half termly, and in other subjects termly. These assessments are recorded on our online assessment programme, which allows us to monitor rates of progress, and to provide timely interventions for any pupils not making expected progress in any area. At Clarendon, we use a bespoke assessment framework based on the age related stages of the National Curriculum and, for pupils working below Stage 1, our own levels based partly on the previous P Scales. Each level and stage are broken down into many smaller units, allowing us to measure progress effectively by percentage increase.
Each half term, pupils complete a given exercise covering a specific area of English or maths which is more formally assessed and annotated, and these pieces of work are added to the pupil’s golden book. These pieces of work are then brought to moderation meetings so that staff can ensure consistency of assessment throughout the school. Moderation meetings are also held with other similar schools to ensure that Clarendon’s assessments are robust.
Each pupil has individual annual academic targets set by staff in September. The teacher assessment targets are based on the Clarendon Flight Path, which uses aggregated data from 4 similar schools, all rated Good or Outstanding by Ofsted. Clarendon’s flight path then uses the upper quartile (top 25% of all the aggregated data) to give us our targets annually and for the end of each Key Stage. Further targets are also set for progress in reading, maths and spelling using our annual standardised tests.
At the end of Key Stage 3, our assessments allow us to guide and advise pupils in their curriculum choices, and to tailor our range of qualifications to provide appropriate challenge to individual pupils.
Pupils in Key Stage 4 will do a range of assessed and accredited courses, which, depending on the individual’s ability, may include GSCE’s, Functional Skills qualifications at Level 1 and Level 2, BTEC Level 1 and Entry Level qualifications, Entry Level Certificates, Unit Awards and ASDAN awards. These qualifications are externally moderated or marked.
In addition to academic assessment, teachers also assess against our life skills curriculum, ensuring progress in practical, independence and social skills.
All pupils will also have individual targets taken from their Education, Health and Care Plan, covering academic, health and independence skills. These are regularly assessed and updated to ensure that progress is made towards outcomes. Governors set whole school targets for pupil progress and outcomes annually.

E-Safety
At Clarendon School, safeguarding our pupils is our absolute highest priority—and this extends entirely to the digital world. We recognise that the internet, apps, and digital technologies are incredible tools for learning, communication, and enrichment. However, we are also acutely aware that pupils with Moderate Learning Difficulties (MLD) and complex needs, including autism, can be particularly vulnerable to online risks.
Our approach to E-Safety is proactive, inclusive, and fully aligned with statutory government guidance, including the latest Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE) and Ofsted requirements. We believe that teaching our pupils how to navigate the online world safely is a vital life skill.
Our Whole-School Approach
Following KCSIE guidelines, we employ a whole-school approach to online safety, ensuring it is woven into both our Safeguarding and Curriculum policies. We focus on protecting and educating pupils regarding the "Four Cs" of online risk:
How We Keep Pupils Safe at School
Support for Parents and Carers
At Clarendon, our Family Engagement Coordinator, Julie Malak, works closely with parents and carers to help extend online safety seamlessly from the classroom into the home environment. Navigating the fast-changing digital landscape can often feel challenging, but Julie provides practical, approachable guidance to help families set healthy boundaries, manage screen time, and protect children online.
How We Support Families
Parental Controls & Technical Setup: Step-by-step guidance on setting up age-appropriate restrictions and parental locks across everyday technology, including smartphones, tablets, and gaming consoles.
Specialist Software Support (Qustodio): Personalised, hands-on support with downloading, installing, and configuring parental management software such as Qustodio. Julie can walk you through the setup process to help filter content and manage screen time effectively.
Half-Termly Newsletter Updates: Sourcing and sharing high-quality safeguarding guides, app safety updates, and advice on emerging digital trends. Julie curates a dedicated, comprehensive online safety feature in every half-termly school newsletter to keep families informed.
'Device Wise' Parent Workshops (In Development): Having recently completed specialist training on the 'Device Wise' framework led by Dr Armitage, Julie is currently planning interactive parent workshops. These sessions will offer actionable strategies for creating balanced family digital agreements, managing screen time, and discussing online risks constructively.
Get in Touch
No question is too small, whether you need technical assistance configuring a new device, setting up monitoring tools, or simply want advice on digital wellbeing. Parents and carers can contact jmalak@clarendon.richmond.sch.uk directly through the school office or catch up with her during our regular parent coffee mornings.
Reporting & Further Help
We know that the online world changes rapidly, and managing what children do on their devices at home can be challenging. Protecting our young people requires a strong partnership between school and home. We encourage parents and carers to maintain open, non-judgmental conversations with their children about what they are doing online. A useful basis for such conversations are the Childnet SMART rules.
If you are a parent, carer or pupil and you are worried about something that has happened online:
To support you at home, we recommend the following trusted resources (many of which have specific advice for supporting children with SEND):
Internet Matters - SEND Hub: Tailored advice for parents of children with learning difficulties and autism.
Thinkuknow: The education programme from CEOP, offering advice for all ages.
NSPCC Online Safety: Excellent guides on setting up parental controls and discussing online safety.
National Online Safety: Up-to-date guides on the latest apps, games, and social media platforms.
